target_customer: Sports fans using iPhone and iPod Touch (free consumer app, no stated payer)
problem: Fans watching games wanted to share the moment with friends, get scores and chat in one place.
business_model: Free consumer app with no confirmed revenue model

founders.name: Vishwas Prabhakara
founders.background_notes: YC profile lists later roles (COO of Digit, VP at Yelp, founder of HoneyHomes.com); timing relative to Fanvibe not stated so not recorded as prior employers.

founders.name: Arthur Chang
founders.background_notes: Described as software engineer, filmmaker and photographer; later YC W15 founder of Priime.

competitors.name: GetGlue
competitors.what: Media check-in app, added sports check-ins in early 2011

competitors.name: ESPN Passport
competitors.what: Free iPhone app to check in at sporting events

competitors.name: Yahoo Sportacular
competitors.what: Sports scores app adding social box scores and check-ins

technical_complexity.rationale: iPhone app with live score feeds and a social layer; data licensing and push were the main work.

defensibility.rationale: Features were copied by Yahoo, ESPN and GetGlue within months.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents shipped sports check-in features in 2010 and 2011; Fanvibe signed to be acquired by beRecruited in June 2011.

market_need_then: Check-in apps were hot in 2010 after Foursquare, and sports fan interaction on phones was an open category, but no spend evidence was found.

branding.domain_note: fanvibe.com now hosts an unrelated live-sports audio product (2026 footer); original ownership unclear.

brand_strength.rationale: No sources on brand beyond product coverage; the name is similar to other Fan-prefixed startups.

outcome_analysis: Fanvibe, previously named FanPulse, was a two person sports check-in app that incumbents like Yahoo and ESPN matched in 2010. It signed to be acquired by beRecruited in June 2011 with its CEO becoming beRecruited CEO and reported about 100,000 users, a team absorption rather than a product win. No funding amounts were found.
notes: Aggregator pages list a seed round dated June 2010 with no amount or investors and about 20K total; unverified, not recorded. TechCrunch headline said Fanvibe signed a letter of intent; PitchBook lists the deal as completed 2011-06-27. fanvibe.com is today a different product. Prabhakara's later roles not used as prior employers. Founder education not found. Completeness pass: the seed dated 2010-06 (one database says 2010-09) rests on aggregators with no amount; CB Insights totals about 20K over 4 rounds.
